Beat 'turn' ('He never sells. At {pay_fee_pct} a year, it pays him {pay_per_period}, every year.') plus beat 'shares' (profits flowing from the business) and the description ('slices of businesses that pay them back every year... pays out 4% a year') present a 4% yearly payout from shares without selling as how shares work. That is wrong in general: a broad US stock index yields about 1-1.3% in dividends in 2026 (S&P 500 ~1.06-1.24%, long-run avg ~1.8%); 4% a year is a withdrawal rate, which means selling. Fix: either say he takes out 4% a year (drop 'never sells'), or keep 'never sells' and use an assumed dividend of ~1.5-2%.

Beats 'grow' and 'turn' state 7% growth and the 4% payout as certainties ('Growing 7% a year, in 30 years your bonus is $38,061'; 'it pays him'), with no 'if'/'say'/'assumed' in voice or on screen; the topic's verify list requires both to read as illustrative assumptions. Fix: e.g. 'If it grows an assumed 7% a year...' and an 'assumed' label on the equation chip.

Minor (not grounds alone): hook 'They spend it' then shows buying shares, which is saving/investing; the payoff contrast ignores that the 30-year-later $1,522 is nominal (worth far less in today's money) and that shares carry risk. Consider one word of risk/'before inflation' if it fits.
